terra.problem: Saying nobody had to knock down a wall first adds a circumstance the verse does not address.
The explanation identifies the Ben-hadad of these fortresses with the king in 1 Kings 15:18, but neither verse establishes that they are the same person.
Comparing the destruction by fire to crumbs makes light of the calamity.
“Wrong passage” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
The verse does not say the warning came before the events in Nebuchadnezzar’s plan.
The absence of gates and bars does not establish that the nation has no protection at all.
The joke about watching sides turns the threatened calamity into a light bakery comparison.
No people dwelling there does not establish that jackals have the place entirely to themselves.
Comparing the scattering of Elam’s people to flour blowing off a counter makes light of their displacement.
The verse says Elam’s people will be scattered, not that the winds will be scattered.
The last two sentences are flat filler rather than an explanation: the throne is not a place, and mentioning an altar and banner adds nothing.
The explanation ends with generic filler: saying an altar is a different thing does not explain the verse.
The explanation repeats the answer without adding a meaningful explanation and sounds generic.
